quoteNotes.jenni-talk-q02: Fresh master-audio checks remain window-dependent: “a customer” occurs in the sentence crop with both decoders and in the clause crop with greedy decoding; “your customer” occurs in the wider crop with both decoders. The clause crop returns no text with beam decoding. Retain the caption’s “a customer” as a draft, but do not mark the exact quote listening-approved.
quoteNotes.joongi-talk-q02: All six fresh master-audio runs render “problem survey” in the disputed sentence. The paired and wider crops separately render “prompt survey” in the preceding sentence, matching the method name on the slide. Parakeet therefore consistently suggests “problem survey” here, but ASR cannot distinguish a spoken slip from an acoustic recognition error. Use “prompt-survey” in the paraphrase and keep the verbatim quote flagged.
quoteNotes.final-panel-q01: Five of six fresh master-audio runs render “women”; the wider crop with greedy decoding instead renders “human”. This changes the earlier impression that Parakeet was stable across contexts. The captions have “humans”. The exact noun remains unresolved, and the respondent is still not individually attributed. Use the paraphrase for reuse.
quoteNotes.mood-q01: Five of six fresh montage-audio runs render “why you’re building this”; one sentence-crop beam run renders “we’re”. In the original industry-Q&A audio, four of six runs render “you’re”, while both tightly cropped clause runs render “we’re”. The existing caption “you’re” is better supported by sentence and wider context, but the pronoun is still sensitive to cropping and needs listening before verbatim reuse.

interpretation: These are repeated context/decoder variants of one ASR model, not independent votes or calibrated probabilities. A stable model rendering does not guarantee the exact spoken word. All four quote flags remain open.
